title: Effects of HRV-Guided vs. Predetermined Block Training on Performance, HRV and Serum Hormones
authors: Nuuttila OP, Nikander A, Polomoshnov D, Laukkanen JA, Häkkinen K
population: Endurance-trained males in an 8-week block of high-intensity aerobic training with running tests
findings: 24 endurance-trained males compared HRV-guided (HRVG) and predetermined (PD) block periodization of high-intensity aerobic training over 8 weeks.
Both groups significantly improved maximal treadmill velocity (Vmax, p < 0.001) and 3000 m running performance (HRVG p < 0.001; PD p = 0.001).
Relative changes in Vmax and countermovement jump were significantly greater in HRVG (p < 0.05).
Nocturnal heart rate decreased in both groups (p < 0.01), but HRV (RMSSD, LF, TP) increased significantly only in HRVG (p < 0.05).
Authors suggest individually HRV-guided block training 'may be more optimal' than predetermined training.
limitations: n = 24, males only, 8 weeks; the abstract gives no between-group significance for 3000 m time; the abstract does not report the number of hard sessions per group; authors' conclusion is tentative.
implications: A second small run-based RCT with the same direction as Vesterinen 2016: HRV-guided block training is at least as good as fixed blocks, not clearly better.
Nocturnal HR fell in both arms, so a falling resting HR trend reflects training adaptation and should not alone be read as readiness.
Male-only evidence: do not claim validation in women.
